items.title: Shirley Lewis Interview, 1969-03-25
items.q: Do you remember him practicing at all? Did he practice around the place? ... Um, sometimes he'd pick up the horn. ... Because a lot of children would come and they'd find it strange but while he did, they don't practice.

ctx.x: Well, she was another one who liked to cook. But age wouldn't permit it. But she tried her best to cook. Especially on Sundays. She felt that you should have a big meal and you should have some kind of dessert. And while she was over here, she tried to do it until one morning her gown caught a fire. So we more or less forbid her to put the stove after that. But she was a quiet person. She stayed to herself a lot. Because she used to pray a lot. She'd lay across her bed and see the rosemary's all the time. And she…
Do you, um, let me ask you something about Jordan. Do you remember him practicing at all? Did he practice around the place? No.

Um, sometimes he'd pick up the horn. And if he wanted to fix a pad or something on it. And after he had glued the pad on or whatever you do to the pad, he'd blow it a while. But for the same practice, no, he never practiced. For the same practice, no, he didn't do that. Because a lot of children would come and they'd find it strange but while he did, they don't practice. So, you know, playing is all. If he hadn't played in a while to get his fingers in order, but for the same practice, no, he didn't do that.…
